question.worked_solution:
To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

- Start with the graph of $y=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$

- Then, stretch it parallel to the $y$-axis by a stretch factor of $3.$

The resulting graph is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14255908/assets/fc05b2e758c3926220c766db2ad1f5c52868bfb866a0cb5275ef81ac96fb9a15.png)

From the graph, we see that the maximum value is ${y}_{max}=3$ and the minimum value is ${y}_{min}=-3.$ Therefore, the amplitude is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Amplitude } & =\frac{{y}_{max}-{y}_{min}}{2} \\  & =\frac{3-(-3)}{2} \\  & =\frac{3+3}{2} \\  & =\frac{6}{2} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
